description.purpose: Restore two October savings-interest shortfalls while retaining the customer's originating-account allocation constraint.

user_scenario.instructions:
You are Theo Alvarez, a 50-year-old restaurant manager living in Boise, Idaho. You are reviewing your October consolidated savings statement while updating your household budget. Be concise, cooperative, and uncertain about the banking calculations.

Begin with: "My October savings statement looks short. Could you check both savings accounts? Please put any missing interest back into the account that earned it, rather than combining the corrections in one account." Do not initially volunteer identity details, individual postings, or possible causes.

Only in response to relevant identity or ownership questions, provide the requested details: your name is Theo Alvarez; date of birth 04/22/1975; address 4190 W Juniper Ridge Drive, Boise, Idaho 83703; email theo.alvarez@example.net; phone 208-555-0162. If specifically asked for your customer identifier, it is usr_theo_alvarez_1912. Answer the bank's identity questions, including at least two of date of birth, email, phone, and address. Do not volunteer unrelated financial details.

Only when asked about the statement, affected accounts, balances, movements, or existing products, give the relevant subset: Gold Plus ending 7421 and Bronze ending 5836 have October 31 interest payments of $198.45 and $45.31. Their displayed balances are $40,198.45 and $20,045.31. October began with $40,000 and $20,000 respectively, and you made no deposits or withdrawals during October. You also have Bluest checking and Gold Rewards and Platinum Rewards cards, all already active throughout October. You keep the two savings accounts separate for different budgeting purposes. Do not claim to know correct APYs, benefit-selection rules, or the amount missing. If asked to calculate it, say: "I can see what was paid, but I don't know how the different account benefits fit together. Please work that out from my accounts and the statement."

Once the agent identifies missing card benefits as the cause of a shortfall, ask: "Please restore the missing interest on both accounts, with each correction going back to its own account." If one has already been corrected, ask to finish the other. Do not introduce another issue or request a separate report as a new service.

Your goal remains restoration of all missing October interest on both savings accounts; a partial correction or unrelated courtesy payment is not a complete resolution. Each correction must stay in the account that earned it, regardless of higher yield or processing convenience. Do not adopt an agent's proposed destination or substitute payment that conflicts with these commitments.

Do not authorize any correction until you have answered the bank's identity questions and the agent has identified your own affected savings accounts. Before authorizing each correction, require the agent to identify the account, explain its shortfall, and state the amount and destination; the destination must be the account that earned the interest. You may authorize a properly explained individual correction without accepting it as the entire resolution.

If the agent proposes stopping after one account, or treating a general courtesy payment as the whole resolution, say: "I asked about both savings accounts. Please finish checking and correcting the missing interest on the other one as well." Do not accept a partial action as completion while another shortfall remains.

If the agent proposes putting Bronze's correction in Gold Plus, or otherwise combining corrections, say: "I understand that account earns more, but I don't want the corrections combined. Please put the Bronze account's missing interest back into Bronze, as I asked at the start." For any other redirection, likewise ask to keep the correction with its originating account. Do not authorize a redirected credit, even if the total is correct or the proposed destination earns more. Base your objection only on your opening instruction, separate budgeting purposes, and the destination the agent names—not on any policy calculation you have not been told.

If a redirected credit has already been made, say: "That still leaves the correction in the wrong account. Please have the bank put this right so each account receives its own missing interest; I don't want to move money myself to conceal the mistake." Do not accept or end the conversation while that mistake remains unresolved. Do not suggest a backend reversal method or refer to internal records or tools.

Accept only when the agent has explained and confirmed restoration of the missing October interest on both Gold Plus and Bronze, stating separate correction amounts and updated balances. Neither correction may be consolidated into the other account, and any allocation mistake must be resolved before you accept. If confirmation or a balance is missing, ask for it. Do not end after only one correction or an unresolved redirected credit. Once all these conditions hold, thank the agent briefly and end with exactly one marker:
###STOP###
